And number two, it is very easy to do this because on MacBook, for example, you can do Control Shift Command 4 and you can draw a window and it copy-pastes that window into a clipboard, and then you can just go to your ChatGPT and you can Control V or Command V to paste it in and you can ask about that. So it's very easy to take chunks of your screen and ask questions about them using this technique.
turns.zh: 我想说的是，第一，注意转录并确保它是正确的。第二，这很容易做到，因为例如在 MacBook 上，你可以按 Control Shift Command 4，然后画一个窗口，它就会把那个窗口复制粘贴到剪贴板，然后你可以直接打开 ChatGPT，用 Control V 或 Command V 粘贴进去，就可以提问了。所以用这个技巧截取屏幕上的部分内容并提问非常容易。

turns.en: And then the other thing I would say about this is that of course this is medical information and you don't want it to be wrong. I will say that in the case of blood test results, I feel more confident trusting ChatGPT a bit more because this is not something esoteric. I do expect there to be tons and tons of documents about blood test results and I do expect that the knowledge of the model is good enough that it kind of understands these numbers, these ranges, and I can tell it more about myself and all this kind of stuff. So I do think that it is quite good, but of course you probably want to talk to an actual doctor as well, but I think this is a really good first draft and something that maybe gives you things to talk about with your doctor, etc.
turns.zh: 然后关于这一点，我想说的另一件事是，当然这是医疗信息，你不希望它出错。我要说的是，在血液检测结果的情况下，我更愿意相信 ChatGPT 一点，因为这不是什么深奥的东西。我确实期望有大量关于血液检测结果的文档，而且我确实期望模型的知识足够好，能够理解这些数字、这些范围，我可以告诉它更多关于我自己的信息等等。所以我确实认为它相当不错，但当然你可能还是想和真正的医生谈谈，不过我认为这是一个非常好的初稿，也许能给你一些和医生讨论的内容等等。

turns.en: Another example is I do a lot of math and code. I found this tricky question in a paper recently, and so I copy-pasted this expression and I asked for it in text because then I can copy this text and I can ask a model what it thinks, um, the value of x evaluated at pi or something like that. It's a trick question. You can try it yourself.
turns.zh: 另一个例子是我做很多数学和代码。我最近在一篇论文中发现了这个棘手的问题，所以我复制粘贴了这个表达式，我要求它以文本形式呈现，因为这样我可以复制这段文本，然后问模型它怎么想，嗯，x 在 pi 处的值之类的。这是一个陷阱题。你可以自己试试。

turns.en: Next example. Here I had a Colgate toothpaste and I was a little bit suspicious about all the ingredients in my Colgate toothpaste and I wanted to know what the hell is all this? So this is Colgate. What the hell is these things? So it transcribed it and then it told me a bit about these ingredients and I thought this was extremely helpful. And then I asked it, okay, which of these would be considered safest and also potentially less safe? And then I asked it, okay, if I only care about the actual function of the toothpaste and I don't really care about other useless things like colors and stuff like that, which of these could we throw out? And it said that, okay, these are the essential functional ingredients and this is a bunch of random stuff you probably don't want in your toothpaste. And basically, spoiler alert, most of the stuff here shouldn't be there. And so it's really upsetting to me that companies put all this stuff in your food or cosmetics and stuff like that when it really doesn't need to be there.
turns.zh: 下一个例子。这里我有一支高露洁牙膏，我对高露洁牙膏中的所有成分有点怀疑，我想知道这到底是什么鬼？所以这是高露洁。这些东西到底是什么鬼？于是它转录了，然后告诉我一些关于这些成分的信息，我觉得这非常有帮助。然后我问它，好吧，这些成分中哪些被认为最安全，哪些可能不太安全？然后我问它，好吧，如果我只关心牙膏的实际功能，而不关心其他无用的东西，比如颜色之类的，哪些可以扔掉？它说，好吧，这些是必要的功能成分，这是一堆你可能不想要在牙膏里的随机东西。基本上，剧透警告，这里的大部分东西都不应该存在。所以公司把这些东西放进你的食物或化妆品之类的东西里，而它们真的不需要在那里，这让我非常不安。

turns.en: The last example I wanted to show you is, so this is not, so this is a meme that I sent to a friend and my friend was confused like oh what is this meme? I don't get it. And I was showing them that ChatGPT can help you understand memes. So I copy-pasted this meme and asked explain and basically this explains the meme that okay multiple crows, a group of crows is called a murderer and so when this crow gets close to that crow it's like an attempted murderer. So yeah was pretty good at explaining this joke.
turns.zh: 我想展示的最后一个例子是，所以这不是，所以这是我发给朋友的一个梗图，我的朋友很困惑，哦，这个梗图是什么？我不明白。我向他们展示 ChatGPT 可以帮助你理解梗图。所以我复制粘贴了这个梗图，并问了解释，基本上它解释了这个梗图，好吧，多只乌鸦，一群乌鸦被称为谋杀，所以当这只乌鸦靠近那只乌鸦时，就像谋杀未遂。所以是的，它很擅长解释这个笑话。

turns.en: And now vice versa, you can get these models to generate images and the OpenAI offering of this is called DALL-E and we're on the third version and it can generate really beautiful images on basically given arbitrary prompts. Is this the Kinkaku-ji temple in Kyoto? I think I visited, so this is really beautiful and so it can generate really stylistic images and you can ask for any arbitrary style of any arbitrary topic etc. Now, I don't actually personally use this functionality way too often. So, I cooked up a random example just to show you, but as an example, where are the big headlines news today? There's a bunch of headlines around politics, health, international entertainment, and so on. And I used search tool for this. And then I said, generate an image that summarizes today. And so, having all of this in the context, we can generate an image like this that kind of summarizes today. Just as an example.
turns.zh: 现在反过来，你可以让这些模型生成图像，OpenAI 提供的这个功能叫做 DALL-E，我们现在是第三个版本，它基本上可以根据任意提示生成非常漂亮的图像。这是京都的金阁寺吗？我想我去过，所以这真的很美，它可以生成非常有风格的图像，你可以要求任何主题的任何风格等等。现在，我个人实际上并不经常使用这个功能。所以我编造了一个随机例子只是为了给你看，但举个例子，今天的大新闻头条是什么？有一堆关于政治、健康、国际娱乐等的头条。我用了搜索工具。然后我说，生成一张总结今天的图像。所以，把所有这些放在上下文中，我们可以生成一张像这样总结今天的图像。只是举个例子。

turns.en: And the way I use this functionality is usually for arbitrary content creation. So as an example when you go to my YouTube channel then this video let's reproduce GPT-2 this image over here was generated using a competitor actually to DALL-E called ideogram.ai and the same for this image that's also generated by ideogram and this image as well was generated I think also by ideogram or this may have been ChatGPT I'm not sure I use some of the tools interchangeably so I use it to generate icons and things like that and you can just kind of ask for whatever you want.
turns.zh: 我使用这个功能的方式通常是用于任意内容创作。举个例子，当你去我的 YouTube 频道，这个视频“让我们复现 GPT-2”，这里的这张图片是用一个实际上与 DALL-E 竞争的叫做 ideogram.ai 生成的，这张图片也是一样，也是由 ideogram 生成的，这张图片也是由 ideogram 生成的，我想，或者这可能是 ChatGPT，我不确定，我互换使用一些工具，所以我用它来生成图标之类的东西，你可以要求任何你想要的东西。

turns.en: Now I will note that the way that this actually works, the image output, it's not done fully in the model, um, currently with DALL-E 3, with DALL-E, this is a separate model that takes text and creates image. And what's actually happening under the hood here in the current iteration of ChatGPT is when I say generate an image that summarizes today, this will actually under the hood create a caption for that image and that caption is sent to a separate model that is an image generator model. And so it's kind of stitched up in this way, but it's not like super important to I think fully understand at this point.
turns.zh: 现在我要指出，这实际上是如何工作的，图像输出，它并不是完全在模型中完成的，嗯，目前使用 DALL-E 3，使用 DALL-E，这是一个单独的模型，接受文本并创建图像。在 ChatGPT 的当前迭代中，实际上在底层发生的事情是，当我说生成一张总结今天的图像时，这实际上会在底层为该图像创建一个标题，然后该标题被发送到一个单独的模型，即图像生成模型。所以它以这种方式拼接起来，但我认为在这一点上完全理解它并不是超级重要。

turns.en: So that is image output. Now, next up, I want to show you an extension where the model can actually see video and this is included in what I showed you previously called advanced voice. It's not available on the web app, but it's available on the mobile app. So, if we go to advanced voice and we connect. So, hello. I'm demonstrating the video capabilities and I'm showing to the camera that there is a little video icon over there. And when you press it, you can basically see you can basically show the model different things.
turns.zh: 所以这就是图像输出。现在，接下来，我想向你展示一个扩展，模型实际上可以看到视频，这包含在我之前向你展示的称为高级语音的功能中。它在网页应用上不可用，但在移动应用上可用。所以，如果我们进入高级语音并连接。所以，你好。我正在演示视频功能，我向摄像头展示那里有一个小视频图标。当你按下它时，你基本上可以看到，你基本上可以向模型展示不同的东西。

turns.en: I can see the camera feed. It looks like you've got some black acoustic foam panels on the wall. Are you testing out how well they reduce echo in the room?
turns.zh: 我能看到摄像头画面。看起来你墙上有些黑色的吸音泡沫板。你是在测试它们减少房间回声的效果吗？

turns.en: Uh, yeah. I was testing out the acoustic foam. Uh, that's right. But it's not actually that helpful.
turns.zh: 呃，是的。我在测试吸音泡沫。呃，没错。但它实际上并没有那么有用。

turns.en: Sometimes placement can make a big difference. Have you tried covering more corners or experimenting with different layouts?
turns.zh: 有时放置位置可以产生很大差异。你试过覆盖更多角落或尝试不同的布局吗？

turns.en: Okay. Well, let's look at this. What book is this? Do you know?
turns.zh: 好的。好吧，让我们看看这个。这是什么书？你知道吗？

turns.en: Yes, that's Genghis Khan and the Making of the Modern World by Jack Weatherford. It's a fascinating book about the impact of Genghis Khan on world history.
turns.zh: 是的，那是杰克·韦瑟福德写的《成吉思汗与现代世界的形成》。这是一本关于成吉思汗对世界历史影响的迷人书籍。

turns.en: Yeah, pretty good. Do you see this other book? What is it?
turns.zh: 是的，相当不错。你看到另一本书了吗？它是什么？

turns.en: That's Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman by Richard Feynman. It's a collection of humorous anecdotes from the physicist's life. It's really entertaining.
turns.zh: 那是理查德·费曼的《别闹了，费曼先生》。这是一本物理学家生活中的幽默轶事集。真的很有趣。

turns.en: And what is this?
turns.zh: 那这是什么？

turns.en: That's an Aranet4, a portable CO2 monitor. It measures carbon dioxide levels, temperature, humidity, and air pressure.
turns.zh: 那是一个 Aranet4，便携式二氧化碳监测器。它测量二氧化碳水平、温度、湿度和气压。

turns.en: It's quite useful for monitoring indoor air quality.
turns.zh: 它对监测室内空气质量相当有用。

turns.en: So, we're currently at 713, right? Do you think that's good or what?
turns.zh: 所以，我们现在是 713，对吧？你觉得这算好吗？

turns.en: A CO2 level of 713 ppm is generally okay. It's normal for indoor spaces. Ideally, you want it below 800 ppm. If it goes above a thousand, you might need more ventilation.
turns.zh: 二氧化碳浓度 713 ppm 通常还可以，对室内空间来说是正常的。理想情况下，你希望它低于 800 ppm。如果超过 1000，你可能需要更多通风。

turns.en: Got it. And how about this map? Do you know what this map is?
turns.zh: 明白了。那这张地图呢？你知道这是什么地图吗？

turns.en: Yes, that looks like a map of Middle Earth from J.R.R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings. It's a great piece for any fan of the series.
turns.zh: 是的，那看起来像是 J.R.R. 托尔金《指环王》中的中土世界地图。对任何该系列的粉丝来说都是很棒的作品。

turns.en: Yeah, good job. Thank you for the demonstration.
turns.zh: 是的，做得好。谢谢你的演示。

turns.en: You're welcome. Glad I could help. If you need anything else, just let me know.
turns.zh: 不客气。很高兴能帮上忙。如果你还需要什么，尽管告诉我。

turns.en: So, that's a brief demo. You basically have the camera running, you can point it at stuff and you can just talk to the model. It is quite magical, super simple to use. I don't personally use it in my daily life because I'm kind of like a power user of all the ChatGPT apps and I don't kind of just like go around pointing at stuff and asking the model for stuff. I usually have very targeted queries about code and programming etc. But I think if I was demonstrating some of this to my parents or my grandparents and have them interact in a very natural way, this is something that I would probably show them because they can just point the camera at things and ask questions. Now, under the hood, I'm not actually 100% sure that they currently consume the video. I think they actually still just take image sections, like maybe they take one image per second or something like that. But from your perspective as a user of the tool, it definitely feels like you can just stream it video and have it make sense. So I think that's pretty cool as a functionality.
turns.zh: 所以，这是一个简短的演示。你基本上让摄像头运行，你可以把它对准东西，然后直接和模型对话。这相当神奇，使用起来超级简单。我个人在日常生活中并不使用它，因为我算是所有 ChatGPT 应用的高级用户，我不会到处指着东西问模型。我通常有关于代码和编程等非常具体的查询。但我想，如果我要向我的父母或祖父母演示其中一些功能，并让他们以非常自然的方式互动，这很可能是我会向他们展示的东西，因为他们可以直接把摄像头对准物体并提问。现在，在底层，我并不完全确定他们目前是否消费视频。我认为他们实际上仍然只是截取图像片段，比如可能每秒截取一帧图像之类的。但从你作为工具用户的角度来看，感觉就像你可以直接流式传输视频并让它理解。所以我认为作为一种功能，这相当酷。

turns.en: And finally, I wanted to briefly show you that there's a lot of tools now that can generate videos and they are incredible and they're very rapidly evolving. I'm not going to cover this too extensively because I think it's relatively self-explanatory. I don't personally use them that much in my work, but that's just because I'm not in a kind of a creative profession or something like that. So, this is a tweet that compares number of AI video generation models as an example. This tweet is from about a month ago, so this may have evolved since, but I just wanted to show you that all of these models were asked to generate, I guess, a tiger in a jungle. And they're all quite good. I think right now V2, I think, is really near state-of-the-art. And really good. Yeah, that's pretty incredible, right? This is open, etc. So, they will all have a slightly different style, different quality, etc. And you can compare and contrast and use some of these tools that are dedicated to this problem.
turns.zh: 最后，我想简要展示一下，现在有很多工具可以生成视频，它们非常惊人，而且发展非常迅速。我不打算过于详细地介绍，因为我认为这相对不言自明。我个人在工作中不太使用它们，但那只是因为我不在创意行业之类的。所以，这是一条推文，举例比较了多个 AI 视频生成模型。这条推文大约是一个月前的，所以可能已经有所发展，但我只是想展示所有这些模型都被要求生成，我猜，丛林中的老虎。它们都相当不错。我认为目前 V2 真的接近最先进水平。真的很好。是的，这相当不可思议，对吧？这是开源的，等等。所以，它们都会有略微不同的风格、不同的质量等。你可以比较和对比，并使用一些专门解决这个问题的工具。

turns.en: Okay. And the final topic I want to turn to is some quality of life features that I think are quite worth mentioning. So the first one I want to talk about is ChatGPT's memory feature. So say you're talking to ChatGPT and you say something like when roughly do you think was peak Hollywood? Now I'm actually surprised that ChatGPT gave me an answer here because I feel like very often these models are very averse to actually having any opinions. They say something along the lines of oh I'm just an AI. I'm here to help. I don't have any opinions and stuff like that. So here actually it seems to have an opinion and says that the last true peak before franchises took over was 1990s to early 2000s. So I actually happen to really agree with ChatGPT here and I really agree. So totally agreed. Now I'm curious what happens here. Okay. So nothing happened. So what you can basically every single conversation like we talked about begins with empty token window and goes until the end. The moment I do new conversation or new chat everything gets wiped clean. But ChatGPT does have an ability to save information from chat to chat but it has to be invoked. So sometimes ChatGPT will trigger it automatically but sometimes you have to ask for it. So basically say something along the lines of can you please remember this or like remember my preference or whatever something like that. So what I'm looking for is I think it's going to work. There we go. So you see this memory updated believes that late 1990s and early 2000 was the greatest peak of Hollywood etc. Um, yeah. So, and then it also went on a bit about 1970. And then it allows you to manage memories. So we'll look into that in a second. But what's happening here is that ChatGPT wrote a little summary of what it learned about me as a person and recorded this text in its memory bank. And a memory bank is basically a separate piece of ChatGPT that is kind of like a database of knowledge about you. And this database of knowledge is always prepended to all the conversations so that the model has access to it. And so I actually really like this because every now and then the memory updates whenever you have conversations with ChatGPT and if you just let this run and you just use ChatGPT naturally then over time it really gets to like know you to some extent and it will start to make references to the stuff that's in the memory. And so when this feature was announced, I wasn't 100% sure if this was going to be helpful or not, but I think I'm definitely coming around and I've used this in a bunch of ways and I definitely feel like ChatGPT is knowing me a little bit better over time and is being a bit more relevant to me and it's all happening just by sort of natural interaction and over time through this memory feature. So sometimes it will trigger it explicitly and sometimes you have to ask for it.
turns.zh: 好的。我想谈的最后一个主题是一些我认为非常值得提及的生活质量功能。所以第一个我想谈的是 ChatGPT 的记忆功能。假设你在和 ChatGPT 对话，你说类似“你觉得好莱坞的巅峰期大概是什么时候？”现在实际上我很惊讶 ChatGPT 在这里给了我一个答案，因为我觉得很多时候这些模型非常不愿意真正持有任何观点。它们会说类似“哦，我只是一个 AI。我在这里帮忙。我没有任何观点”之类的话。所以这里它似乎确实有观点，说在系列电影接管之前的最后一个真正巅峰是 1990 年代到 2000 年代初。所以我实际上碰巧非常同意 ChatGPT 在这里的观点，我真的很同意。所以完全同意。现在我很想知道这里会发生什么。好的。所以什么都没发生。所以基本上每一次对话，就像我们谈到的，都从空的 token 窗口开始，一直持续到最后。当我进行新对话或新聊天时，一切都会被清除。但 ChatGPT 确实有能力在聊天之间保存信息，但必须被调用。所以有时 ChatGPT 会自动触发它，但有时你必须要求它。所以基本上说类似“你能请记住这个”或“记住我的偏好”之类的话。所以我在寻找的是，我认为它会起作用。好了。所以你看这个记忆更新了，认为 1990 年代末和 2000 年代初是莱坞的最大巅峰等等。嗯，是的。所以，然后它还继续谈了一点 1970 年。然后它允许你管理记忆。所以我们稍后会研究一下。但这里发生的是，ChatGPT 写了一个关于它对我这个人的了解的简短总结，并将这段文本记录在它的记忆库中。记忆库基本上是 ChatGPT 的一个独立部分，有点像关于你的知识数据库。而这个知识数据库总是被前置到所有对话中，以便模型可以访问它。所以我实际上真的很喜欢这个，因为每当你与 ChatGPT 对话时，记忆会不时更新，如果你只是让它运行，自然地使用 ChatGPT，那么随着时间的推移，它真的会在某种程度上了解你，并开始引用记忆中的内容。所以当这个功能宣布时，我并不 100% 确定这是否有帮助，但我认为我肯定在逐渐接受，我已经以多种方式使用了它，我确实觉得 ChatGPT 随着时间的推移越来越了解我，对我越来越相关，而这一切都只是通过自然的互动和随着时间的推移通过这个记忆功能发生的。所以有时它会明确触发，有时你必须要求它。

turns.en: Okay, now I thought I was going to show you some of the memories and how to manage them. But actually, I just looked and it's a little too personal, honestly. So, it's just a database. It's a list of little text strings. Those text strings just make it to the beginning and you can edit the memories, which I really like. And you can, you know, add memories, delete memories, manage your memories database. So, that's incredible. I will also mention that I think the memory feature is unique to ChatGPT. I think that other LLMs currently do not have this feature. And I will also say that for example, ChatGPT is very good at movie recommendations and so I actually think that having this in its memory will help it create better movie recommendations for me. So that's pretty cool. The next thing I wanted to briefly show is custom instructions. So you can to a very large extent modify your ChatGPT and how you like it to speak to you. And so I quite appreciate that as well.
turns.zh: 好的，现在我以为我会向你们展示一些记忆以及如何管理它们。但实际上，我刚看了一下，说实话，这有点太个人化了。所以，它只是一个数据库。它是一个小文本字符串的列表。那些文本字符串只是被放到开头，你可以编辑记忆，我真的很喜欢这一点。而且你可以，你知道，添加记忆、删除记忆、管理你的记忆数据库。所以，这太不可思议了。我还要提到，我认为记忆功能是 ChatGPT 独有的。我认为其他 LLM 目前没有这个功能。我还要说，例如，ChatGPT 非常擅长电影推荐，所以我实际上认为在它的记忆中拥有这些将帮助它为我创建更好的电影推荐。所以这很酷。接下来我想简要展示的是自定义指令。所以你可以在很大程度上修改你的 ChatGPT 以及你希望它如何与你交谈。所以我也非常欣赏这一点。

turns.en: You can come to settings, customize ChatGPT, and you see here it says what traits should ChatGPT have. I just told it: don't be like an HR business partner, just talk to me normally. Also, I love explanations, education, insights, etc., so be educational whenever you can. You can type anything here and experiment with that a little bit. I also experimented with telling it my identity. I'm just experimenting with this. I'm also learning Korean, so here I am telling it that when it gives me Korean, it should use this tone of formality. Otherwise, sometimes it might give me the informal or way too formal tone, and I just want this tone by default. So that's an example of something I added. Anything you want to modify about ChatGPT globally between conversations, you put it here into your custom instructions. I quite welcome this. I think you can do this with many other LLMs as well. Look for it somewhere in the settings.
turns.zh: 你可以进入设置，自定义 ChatGPT，这里写着 ChatGPT 应该具备哪些特质。我就告诉它：别像个 HR 业务伙伴，正常跟我说话就行。另外，我喜欢解释、教育、见解等等，所以尽可能提供教育性内容。你可以在这里输入任何内容，稍微实验一下。我还实验了告诉它我的身份。我只是在尝试这个。我也在学韩语，所以这里我告诉它，当它给我韩语时，应该使用这种正式语气。否则，有时它可能给我非正式或过于正式的语气，而我只想要默认这种语气。所以这是我添加的一个例子。任何你想在对话之间全局修改 ChatGPT 的地方，你都可以放在这里的自定义指令中。我很欢迎这个功能。我认为你也可以用许多其他 LLM 做到这一点。在设置里找找看。

turns.en: The last feature I wanted to cover is custom GPTs, which I use once in a while. I like to use them specifically for language learning the most. Let me give you an example of how I use these. Let me first show you—maybe they show up on the left here. Let me show you this one for example, Korean detailed translator. No, sorry, I want to start with this one: Korean vocabulary extractor. Basically, the idea here is I give it—this is a custom GPT—I give it a sentence and it extracts vocabulary in dictionary form. So here for example, given this sentence, this is the vocabulary, and notice that it's in the format of Korean semicolon English, and this can be copy-pasted into Anki flashcards app. This means that it's very easy to turn a sentence into flashcards. Now the way this works is basically if we just go under the hood and we go to edit GPT, you can see that this is all just done via prompting. Nothing special is happening here. The important thing here is instructions. So when I pop this open, I just explain a little bit of background information: I'm learning Korean, I'm a beginner. Instructions: I will give you a piece of text and I want you to extract the vocabulary, and then I give it some example output. Basically, I'm being detailed. When I give instructions to LLMs, I always like to number one give it the description, but then also give it examples. I like to give concrete examples. So here are four concrete examples. What I'm doing here really is constructing what's called a few-shot prompt. So I'm not just describing a task, which is like asking for performance in a zero-shot manner, just do it without examples. I'm giving it a few examples, and this is now a few-shot prompt. I find that this always increases the accuracy of LLMs. That's a general good strategy. Then when you update and save this LLM, then given a single sentence it does that task. Notice that there's nothing new and special going on. All I'm doing is saving myself a little bit of work because I don't have to start from scratch and describe the whole setup in detail. I don't have to tell ChatGPT all of this each time. What this feature really is is that it's just saving you prompting time. If there's a certain prompt that you keep reusing, then instead of reusing that prompt and copy-pasting it over and over again, just create a custom GPT, save that prompt a single time, and then what's changing per use of it is the different sentence. If I give it a sentence, it always performs this task. This is helpful if there are certain prompts or certain tasks that you always reuse.
turns.zh: 我想介绍的最后一个功能是自定义 GPT，我偶尔会用。我最喜欢专门用它们来学习语言。让我举个例子说明我如何使用这些。先给你看看——它们可能显示在左边这里。让我展示这个，例如，韩语详细翻译器。不，抱歉，我想从这个开始：韩语词汇提取器。基本上，这里的想法是我给它——这是一个自定义 GPT——我给它一个句子，它提取词典形式的词汇。例如，给定这个句子，这是词汇，注意它的格式是韩语分号英语，这可以复制粘贴到 Anki 闪卡应用。这意味着很容易把句子变成闪卡。现在它的工作原理基本上是，如果我们深入底层，去编辑 GPT，你可以看到这一切都是通过提示完成的。这里没有什么特别的事情发生。重要的是指令。所以当我打开这个，我只是解释一点背景信息：我在学韩语，我是初学者。指令：我会给你一段文本，我希望你提取词汇，然后我给它一些示例输出。基本上，我很详细。当我给 LLM 指令时，我总是喜欢首先给出描述，但然后也给出例子。我喜欢给出具体的例子。所以这里有四个具体的例子。我在这里真正做的是构建所谓的少样本提示。所以我不只是描述一个任务，这就像以零样本方式要求性能，只是没有例子就做。我给它几个例子，这就是少样本提示。我发现这总是提高 LLM 的准确性。我认为这是一个普遍的好策略。然后当你更新并保存这个 LLM，然后给定一个句子，它就会执行那个任务。注意这里没有什么新的和特别的事情发生。我所做的只是节省一点工作，因为我不必从头开始并详细描述整个设置。我不必每次告诉 ChatGPT 所有这些。这个功能真正做的是节省你的提示时间。如果有一个你不断重复使用的提示，那么与其重复使用那个提示并一遍又一遍地复制粘贴，不如创建一个自定义 GPT，保存那个提示一次，然后每次使用它时改变的是不同的句子。如果我给它一个句子，它总是执行这个任务。如果你总是重复使用某些提示或某些任务，这很有帮助。

turns.en: The next example that I think transfers to every other language would be basic translation. As an example, I have this sentence in Korean and I want to know what it means. Many people will go to Google Translate or something like that. Google Translate is famously not very good with Korean. So a lot of people use Naver or Papago and so on. If you put that here, it kind of gives you a translation. These translations often are okay as a translation, but I don't actually really understand how this sentence goes to this translation. Where are the pieces? I want to know more and I want to be able to ask clarifying questions and so on. Here it kind of breaks it up a little bit, but it's just not as good because a bunch of it gets omitted, right? Those are usually particles and so on. So I basically built a much better translator in ChatGPT and I think it works significantly better. I have a Korean detailed translator. When I put that same sentence here, I get what I think is a much, much better translation. So, it's 3 in the afternoon now, and I want to go to my favorite cafe. And this is how it breaks up, and I can see exactly how all the pieces of it translate part by part into English. So, Chigamin, afternoon, etc. All of this. What's really beautiful about this is not only can I see all the little detail of it, but I can ask clarifying questions right here and we can just follow up and continue the conversation. This is significantly better in translation than anything else you can get. If you're learning a different language, I would not use a different translator other than ChatGPT. It understands a ton of nuance. It understands slang. It's extremely good. I don't know why translators even exist at this point. I think GPT is just so much better.
turns.zh: 下一个我认为可以转移到任何其他语言的例子是基本翻译。举个例子，我有这个韩语句子，我想知道它是什么意思。许多人会去 Google 翻译或类似的东西。Google 翻译以对韩语不擅长而闻名。所以很多人使用 Naver 或 Papago 等等。如果你把它放在这里，它会给你一个翻译。这些翻译通常作为翻译还可以，但我实际上并不真正理解这个句子如何变成这个翻译。各个部分在哪里？我想知道更多，并且能够提出澄清问题等等。这里它稍微分解了一下，但就是不够好，因为很多部分被省略了，对吧？那些通常是助词等等。所以我基本上在 ChatGPT 中构建了一个更好的翻译器，我认为它工作得明显更好。我有一个韩语详细翻译器。当我把同一个句子放在这里，我得到了我认为好得多的翻译。所以，现在是下午 3 点，我想去我最喜欢的咖啡馆。这就是它分解的方式，我可以看到它的所有部分如何逐部分翻译成英语。所以，Chigamin，下午，等等。所有这些。真正美妙的是，我不仅可以看到所有细节，还可以在这里提出澄清问题，我们可以继续对话。这比你能得到的任何其他翻译都要好得多。如果你在学习不同的语言，我不会使用 ChatGPT 以外的翻译器。它理解大量的细微差别。它理解俚语。它非常出色。我不知道为什么翻译器还存在。我认为 GPT 好多了。

turns.en: The way this works, if we go here and edit this GPT, just so we can see briefly, these are the instructions that I gave it: You'll be given a sentence in Korean. Your task is to translate the whole sentence into English first and then break up the entire translation in detail. Here again, I'm creating a few-shot prompt. Here is how I gave it the examples because they're a bit more extended. I used an XML-like language just so that the model understands that example one begins here and ends here. I'm using XML tags. Here's the input I gave it and here's the desired output. I just give it a few examples and I specify them in detail. Then I have a few more instructions here. I think this is actually very similar to how you might teach a human a task.
turns.zh: 它的工作原理是，如果我们去这里编辑这个 GPT，简单看一下，这些是我给它的指令：你将得到一个韩语句子。你的任务是先将整个句子翻译成英语，然后详细分解整个翻译。这里再次，我正在创建一个少样本提示。这里是我如何给它例子的，因为它们更扩展一些。我使用了一种类似 XML 的语言，只是为了让模型理解示例 1 从这里开始，到这里结束。我使用 XML 标签。这是我给它的输入，这是期望的输出。我只是给它几个例子，并详细指定它们。然后我还有一些指令在这里。我认为这实际上非常类似于你如何教一个人一项任务。

turns.en: You can explain in words what they're supposed to be doing, but it's so much better if you show them by example how to perform the task. And humans, I think, can also learn in a few-shot manner significantly more efficiently. So you can program this in whatever way you like, and then you get a custom translator that is designed just for you and is a lot better than what you would find on the internet. Empirically, I find that ChatGPT is quite good at translation, especially for a basic beginner like me right now.
turns.zh: 你可以用语言解释它们应该做什么，但如果你通过示例展示如何执行任务，效果会好得多。而且我认为人类也能以少样本的方式更高效地学习。所以你可以按自己喜欢的方式编程，然后得到一个专为你设计的自定义翻译器，比你在网上找到的要好得多。根据经验，我发现 ChatGPT 在翻译方面相当不错，尤其对像我这样的初学者来说。

turns.en: Okay. And maybe the last one that I'll show you, just because I think it ties a bunch of functionality together, is as follows. Sometimes I'm, for example, watching some Korean content. And here we see we have subtitles, but the subtitles are baked into the video, into the pixels. So I don't have direct access to the subtitles. And so what I can do here is I can just screenshot this. And this is a scene between Ginyong and Sulki in Singles Inferno. So I can just take it and I can paste it here. And then this custom GPT I called Korean cap first OCRs it, then it translates it, and then it breaks it down. And so it basically does that, and then I can continue watching, and anytime I need help, I will copy-paste this screenshot here, and this will basically do that translation. And if we look at it under the hood in edit GPT, you'll see that in the instructions, it just simply gives out, it just breaks down the instructions. So you'll be given an image crop from a TV show Singles Inferno, but you can change this, of course. And it shows a tiny piece of dialogue. So I'm giving the model sort of a heads-up and a context for what's happening. And these are the instructions. So first OCR it, then translate it, and then break it down. And then you can do whatever output format you like, and you can play with this and improve it. But this is just a simple example, and this works pretty well. So yeah, these are the kinds of custom GPTs that I've built for myself. A lot of them have to do with language learning. And the way you create these is you come here and you click my GPTs, and you basically create a GPT, and you can configure it arbitrarily here. And as far as I know, GPTs are fairly unique to ChatGPT, but I think some of the other LLM apps probably have similar functionality. So you may want to look for it in the project settings.
turns.zh: 好的。也许我要展示的最后一个，因为我觉得它把一堆功能结合在了一起，是这样的。有时我在看一些韩语内容。这里我们看到有字幕，但字幕是嵌入视频像素中的。所以我无法直接访问字幕。那么我能做的就是截屏。这是《单身即地狱》中 Ginyong 和 Sulki 之间的场景。所以我可以截屏并粘贴到这里。然后这个我称为 Korean cap 的自定义 GPT 会先进行 OCR，然后翻译，再分解。基本上就是这样，然后我可以继续观看，任何时候需要帮助，我就复制粘贴这个截图到这里，它就会完成翻译。如果我们深入查看，在 edit GPT 中，你会看到在指令中，它只是简单地分解了指令。所以你会收到一张来自电视节目《单身即地狱》的图像裁剪，当然你可以更改。它展示了一小段对话。所以我给模型一个提示和上下文，说明正在发生什么。这些是指令。首先 OCR，然后翻译，再分解。然后你可以选择任何输出格式，你可以调整并改进。但这只是一个简单的例子，效果很好。所以是的，这些就是我为自己构建的自定义 GPT。很多都与语言学习有关。创建这些的方法是，你来到这里，点击我的 GPT，然后创建一个 GPT，你可以在这里任意配置。据我所知，GPT 是 ChatGPT 独有的，但我认为其他一些 LLM 应用可能也有类似的功能。所以你可能需要在项目设置中寻找。

turns.en: Okay. So I could go on and on about covering all the different features that are available in ChatGPT and so on. But I think this is a good introduction and a good bird's-eye view of what's available right now, what people are introducing, and what to look out for. So in summary, there is a rapidly growing, changing, shifting, and thriving ecosystem of LLM apps like ChatGPT. ChatGPT is the first and the incumbent and is probably the most feature-rich out of all of them. But all of the other ones are very rapidly growing and becoming either reaching feature parity or even overcoming ChatGPT in some specific cases. As an example, ChatGPT now has internet search, but I still go to Perplexity because Perplexity was doing search for a while and I think their models are quite good. Also, if I want to prototype some simple web apps and I want to create diagrams and stuff like that, I really like Claude artifacts, which is not a feature of ChatGPT. If I just want to talk to a model, then I think ChatGPT advanced voice is quite nice today. And if it's being too PG with you, then you can switch to Grok, things like that. So basically, all the different apps have some strengths and weaknesses, but I think ChatGPT by far is a very good default and the incumbent and most feature-rich.
turns.zh: 好的。我可以继续讲下去，涵盖 ChatGPT 中所有可用的不同功能等等。但我认为这是一个很好的介绍，也是一个很好的鸟瞰图，展示了当前可用的功能、人们正在引入的功能以及需要注意的事项。总之，像 ChatGPT 这样的 LLM 应用生态系统正在快速增长、变化、转变和繁荣。ChatGPT 是第一个，也是现任者，可能是所有应用中最功能丰富的。但所有其他应用都在非常迅速地增长，要么达到功能对等，甚至在某些特定情况下超越 ChatGPT。例如，ChatGPT 现在有互联网搜索，但我仍然去 Perplexity，因为 Perplexity 做搜索已经有一段时间了，我认为他们的模型相当不错。另外，如果我想原型设计一些简单的 Web 应用，并且想创建图表之类的东西，我非常喜欢 Claude artifacts，这不是 ChatGPT 的功能。如果我只是想和模型对话，那么我认为 ChatGPT 的高级语音今天相当不错。如果它对你太谨慎，那么你可以切换到 Grok 之类的。所以基本上，所有不同的应用都有一些优点和缺点，但我认为 ChatGPT 到目前为止是一个非常好的默认选择，是现任者，也是功能最丰富的。

turns.en: Okay, what are some of the things that we are keeping track of when we're thinking about these apps and between their features? So the first thing to realize and that we looked at is you're talking basically to a zip file. Be aware of what pricing tier you're at and depending on the pricing tier, which model you are using. If you are using a model that is very large, that model is going to have basically a lot of world knowledge and it's going to be able to answer complex questions. It's going to have very good writing. It's going to be a lot more creative in its writing and so on. If the model is very small, then probably it's not going to be as creative. It has a lot less world knowledge and it will make mistakes. For example, it might hallucinate. On top of that, a lot of people are very interested in these models that are thinking and trained with reinforcement learning, and this is the latest frontier in research today. So in particular, we saw that this is very useful and gives additional accuracy in problems like math, code, and reasoning. So try without reasoning first, and if your model is not solving that kind of a problem, try to switch to a reasoning model and look for that in the user interface. On top of that, then we saw that we are rapidly giving the models a lot more tools. So, as an example, we can give them an internet search. So, if we're talking about some fresh information or knowledge that is probably not in the zip file, then you actually want to use an internet search tool. And not all of these apps have it. In addition, you may want to give it access to a Python interpreter so that it can write programs. So, for example, if you want to generate figures or plots and show them, you may want to use something like advanced data analysis. If you're prototyping some kind of a web app, you might want to use artifacts. Or if you are generating diagrams because it's right there and inline inside the app. Or if you're programming professionally, you may want to turn to a different app like Cursor and Composer. On top of all of this, there's a layer of multimodality that is rapidly becoming more mature as well and that you may want to keep track of. So we were talking about both the input and the output of all the different modalities, not just text, but also audio, images, and video. And we talked about the fact that some of these modalities can be sort of handled natively inside the language model. Sometimes these models are called omni-models or multimodal models. So they can be handled natively by the language model, which is going to be a lot more powerful, or they can be tacked on as a separate model that communicates with the main model through text or something like that. So that's a distinction to also sometimes keep track of. And on top of all this, we also talked about quality of life features. So for example, file uploads, memory features, instructions, GPTs, and all this kind of stuff. And maybe the last sort of piece that we saw is that all of these apps have usually a web interface that you can go to on your laptop or also a mobile app available on your phone.
turns.zh: 好的，当我们考虑这些应用及其功能时，我们需要关注哪些方面？首先，要意识到我们基本上是在和一个 zip 文件对话。注意你处于哪个定价层级，以及根据定价层级你使用的是哪个模型。如果你使用的是非常大的模型，那个模型基本上会有很多世界知识，能够回答复杂问题。它的写作会非常好，会更有创造力，等等。如果模型非常小，那么它可能不会那么有创造力。它的世界知识少得多，会犯错误。例如，它可能会产生幻觉。此外，很多人对这些经过强化学习训练的思考模型非常感兴趣，这是当今研究的最新前沿。特别是，我们看到这在数学、代码和推理等问题上非常有用，并能提供额外的准确性。所以先尝试不使用推理，如果你的模型无法解决这类问题，尝试切换到推理模型，并在用户界面中寻找。此外，我们还看到我们正在迅速给模型提供更多工具。例如，我们可以给它们互联网搜索。所以，如果我们谈论的是一些新鲜信息或可能不在 zip 文件中的知识，那么你实际上想使用互联网搜索工具。并非所有应用都有这个功能。此外，你可能想给它访问 Python 解释器的权限，以便它可以编写程序。例如，如果你想生成图表或绘图并展示它们，你可能想使用高级数据分析之类的功能。如果你在原型设计某种 Web 应用，你可能想使用 artifacts。或者如果你在生成图表，因为它就在应用内联。或者如果你在进行专业编程，你可能想转向不同的应用，如 Cursor 和 Composer。在所有这些之上，还有一层多模态性，它也在迅速成熟，你可能想关注。所以我们谈论了所有不同模态的输入和输出，不仅仅是文本，还有音频、图像和视频。我们谈到了其中一些模态可以在语言模型内部原生处理。有时这些模型被称为全能模型或多模态模型。所以它们可以由语言模型原生处理，这会强大得多，或者它们可以作为单独的模型附加，通过文本或其他方式与主模型通信。所以这也是有时需要关注的区分。在所有这些之上，我们还谈到了生活质量功能。例如，文件上传、记忆功能、指令、GPT 等等。也许我们看到的最后一点是，所有这些应用通常都有一个 Web 界面，你可以在笔记本电脑上访问，或者也有手机上的移动应用。

turns.en: And we saw that many of these features might be available on the app, in the browser, but not on the phone, and vice versa. So that's also something to keep track of. So all of this is a little bit of a zoo. It's a little bit crazy, but these are the kinds of features that exist.
turns.zh: 我们看到，很多这些功能可能在应用里、在浏览器里能用，但在手机上却不能用，反过来也一样。所以这也是需要留意的一点。所以这一切有点像个动物园，有点疯狂，但这些就是目前存在的各类功能。

consensus.en: LLMs are lossy zip files of the internet with a knowledge cutoff.
consensus.zh: 大语言模型是互联网的有损压缩包，存在知识截止日期。

consensus.en: Post-training shapes the assistant persona; pre-training provides knowledge.
consensus.zh: 后训练塑造助手人格，预训练提供知识。

consensus.en: Thinking models use reinforcement learning to improve math and code accuracy.
consensus.zh: 思考模型通过强化学习提升数学和代码准确性。

consensus.en: Tool use like search and Python interpreter extends model capabilities.
consensus.zh: 搜索和Python解释器等工具使用扩展了模型能力。

consensus.en: Context window is working memory; keep it short for speed and accuracy.
consensus.zh: 上下文窗口是工作记忆，保持简短以提高速度和准确性。

consensus.en: Voice input and custom instructions enhance daily LLM interaction.
consensus.zh: 语音输入和自定义指令增强日常大语言模型交互。

contrarian.en: Models don't do math; they rely on tools or hallucinate results.
contrarian.zh: 模型不做数学，它们依赖工具或幻觉结果。

contrarian.en: Bigger models aren't always better; smaller ones can suffice for simple tasks.
contrarian.zh: 更大的模型并不总是更好，较小的模型足以处理简单任务。

contrarian.en: Deep research outputs are first drafts, not guaranteed accurate.
contrarian.zh: 深度研究输出是初稿，不保证准确。

contrarian.en: Advanced voice mode is often too cautious and refuses many requests.
contrarian.zh: 高级语音模式往往过于谨慎，拒绝许多请求。

contrarian.en: Don't type; use voice for most queries to save time.
contrarian.zh: 不要打字，大多数查询使用语音以节省时间。

contrarian.en: Custom GPTs are just saved prompts, not new models.
contrarian.zh: 自定义GPT只是保存的提示，不是新模型。
